how to be dangerously
well educated
Learn the big timeline of history. Ancient Egypt, Greece, Rome, the Middle Ages, the Renaissance, the World Wars. Everything else hangs on that structure.
Read one classic novel every season. Dostoevsky, Hemingway, Steinbeck. Great stories teach you about people in a way facts never will.
Learn basic economics. Inflation, interest rates, supply and demand. Understanding money makes the news and your own life much clearer.
Visit museums with a plan. Pick one room or one artist and learn the story behind it. Depth beats rushing through ten rooms.
Make learning daily. I do five minutes a day of history, art or science, and over months it builds a real, wide education. Ten minutes a day is enough.
slides.texte_sophia: I do five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. History, art, science. Over months it builds a real, wide education.

slides.texte_overlay: Learn the basics of philosophy. Socrates, the Stoics, Descartes. Philosophy teaches you how to think, not just what to think.
Watch documentaries instead of random videos. Same couch, same time, but you end the evening knowing how the world works. One documentary a week adds up fast.
